To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the systemic administration of a lentiviral NPY-apo B vector effectively reverses the neuronal and glia pathology of AD in the brain and also increases NPC proliferation in the hippocampus.
systemic delivery of a lentiviral expressing NPY-apo-B to APP transgenic mouse brain reverses the neurodegeneration associated with Aβ pathology.

(i) NPY-apo B effectively reverses neurodegeneration and improves cognition in an AD mouse model and (ii) the neuroprotective and behavioral benefits are associated with a significant increase in the number of proliferative NPCs.

developing new treatments for Alzheimer's Disease (AD), a neurodegenerative disease affecting millions of people.
developing new therapies to prevent and/or reverse the pathology of Alzheimer disease.
understanding and treating neurodegenerative diseases.

this study provides evidence that the neuroprotective and regenerative effects of NPY can be exploited for the treatment of AD.

The main takeaway from our work is that
NPY is neuroprotective and can increase NPC proliferation in a mouse model of AD and that this effect is likely mediated by the Y1 and Y5 receptors.
NPY is a potent neuroprotective and regenerative factor that could be used to treat AD and perhaps other neurodegenerative diseases.
